title: Théorie des cycles algébriques : conjectures de Hodge, Tate, Lefschetz, Weil : notes manuscrites (s.d.), lettre (1965).

deep.reconstruction:
Top of page (end of Remarque 1.8, relative version of 1.1/1.7). X and Y are smooth projective with geometrically connected fibres over an arbitrary base S, and Z ∈ CK^n(X ×_S Y) is a K-theoretic cycle class. Suppose the Albanese scheme A_Y of Y/S exists, and we are given a morphism from X into a 'parabelian' scheme, i.e. a torsor under an abelian scheme A. Then Z yields a homomorphism of abelian schemes A_Y → A. It is encoded by a divisorial class on A_Y × A^*, an element of CK^1(A_Y, A^*). This uses Hom(A_Y, A) = Hom(A_Y, A^**), i.e. biextensions / Poincaré classes. On geometric fibres it reduces to the construction already made over a field.

Section 2, 'Application: algebraicity of certain homomorphisms of abelian varieties by means of ℓ-adic cohomology'.

Prop. 2.1. Let X, Y be smooth projective connected over k (algebraically closed), of dimensions n and m. Let Z ∈ Cyc_1(X×Y) be a 1-cycle, i.e. of codimension n+m−1. Then there is a unique homomorphism u: B_X = Pic^{00}_{X/k} (Picard variety) → A_Y (Albanese variety). It is characterized as follows: for every divisor D on X algebraically equivalent to 0 such that the 0-cycle ᵗZ(D) = pr_{2*}((D×Y)·Z) is defined, u(cl D) = S_Y(ᵗZ(D)), where S_Y sums 0-cycles of degree 0 in A_Y.

Next page: u is also characterized ℓ-adically. Under H^1(A_Y) ≅ H^1(Y) (mod torsion) and ψ_X: H^{2n−1}(X)(n−1) → H^1(B_X), the map u^{(1)} is the correspondence action of cl(Z) ∈ H^{2(n+m−1)}(X×Y)(n+m−1). Hence u depends only on the numerical class of Z.

Proof sketch. The composite of the three cohomological maps is induced by algebraic correspondences, independently of ℓ. Cor. 1.7 (a map on H^1 comes from an algebraic cycle iff it is u^{(1)} for a homomorphism of abelian varieties) gives u. A moving lemma then gives the formula on divisors.

This is the classical theory of the homomorphism Pic^0(X) → Alb(Y) induced by a correspondence (Weil, Matsusaka, Lang), recast in Grothendieck's ℓ-adic / motivic framework of the standard conjectures, presumably as groundwork for the H^1 case of the Lefschetz/Hodge-type conjectures.
errors: No substantive error on this page. The margin note 'échanger les rôles de X et Y ?' signals uncertainty about which direction/transposition is natural: the map goes B_X → A_Y via ᵗZ, while the diagram on the next page runs H^1(Y) → H^{2n−1}(X).

Next page: in the proof the composite is written ψ_X a(γ(ξ)) φ_X^{(1)}. Consistency with the diagram requires (φ_Y^{(1)})^{-1}, which is only an isomorphism mod torsion. So the argument works after tensoring with Q_ℓ, or up to torsion.

ideas.what: Homomorphism Pic^0(X) → Alb(Y) induced by a 1-cycle correspondence on X×Y, via D ↦ S_Y(pr_{2*}((D×Y)·Z))
ideas.modern_name: action of correspondences on Picard/Albanese varieties
ideas.usually_credited_to: Weil (Variétés abéliennes et courbes algébriques, 1948), Matsusaka, Lang (Abelian Varieties, 1959)
ideas.where_published: Treated in Kleiman's 'Algebraic cycles and the Weil conjectures' (Dix exposés, 1968), which reports Grothendieck's program

ideas.what: ℓ-adic characterization of u through the cohomology class of Z on H^1, so that u depends only on the homological/numerical class of Z
ideas.modern_name: H^1 part of correspondences; numerical = homological equivalence for the Picard/Albanese motive
ideas.usually_credited_to: Matsusaka (numerical vs algebraic equivalence of divisors), Lieberman 1968, Kleiman 1968
ideas.where_published: Grothendieck, 'Standard conjectures on algebraic cycles' (1969) alludes to the H^1 case; details in Kleiman's Dix exposés

ideas.what: Relative version over a base S: K-theoretic cycle classes CK^n(X×_S Y) induce homomorphisms of Albanese schemes into abelian schemes (with torsors called 'parabelian schemes'), encoded by an element of CK^1(A_Y, A^*)
ideas.modern_name: relative Albanese / correspondences of abelian schemes via divisorial correspondences (biextensions)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck (FGA Picard scheme; SGA 7 biextensions); relative Albanese in later literature
ideas.where_published: Ingredients in FGA (Picard scheme) and SGA 7 VII–VIII (biextensions); this specific statement unsure

deep.surprise_reason: The page records a classical result (correspondences inducing Pic^0 → Alb, with an ℓ-adic characterization) in Grothendieck's standard-conjectures framework. The relative remark using K-theoretic cycles and 'parabelian schemes' is a mildly interesting terminological/organizational detail, but not a new result.
transcription_corrections: 'via un élément de CH^1(A_Y, A^*)' is more likely 'CK^1(A_Y, A^*)'. The K-theoretic notation CK used on the previous page matches the handwriting.
'à l'aide de cohomologie l-adique' probably reads 'au moyen de cohomologie l-adique'.
'de dim n resp. m' is written as 'de dim n, m' on the page.
In the crossed-out lines, 'principal homog.' is replaced by 'schéma parabélien)'. The opening parenthesis belongs before 'sous un schéma abélien A'.
